text: The RTX PRO 6000 queue has the most free capacity and needs the newest software. In one measurement, 58 of its 64 GPUs were idle while the A100 queue had 900 jobs pending against 10 free GPUs. The reason it is idle is that the card is sm_120 and the conda environments' PyTorch only ships kernels to sm_90 — it runs via driver PTX JIT, but nothing is precompiled. Measured cost of that on a small fp32 CNN: one-time ~85 s JIT hit, then ~5% slower than A100 in steady state. Fine for single-GPU work; it has no NVLink/InfiniBand, so never for multi-GPU or multi-node.

Slack messages always go to the user by default. When asked to "send a slack message", "draft a message", or similar, send/draft it as a DM to the user themselves so they can review and forward. NEVER send directly to another person (collaborators, channels, etc.) unless the user explicitly says "send to <person>" or "post in <channel>". Even then, confirm with the user before sending.

Never install packages into a conda env while a cluster job using that env is still running. Check `bjobs` first. If a job is live, either wait for it or `mamba create -n <env>_v2 --clone <env>` and install into the clone. pip can silently replace numpy or scipy on disk underneath the live Python process: modules already imported stay in memory, but anything imported afterwards may load the new version. After ANY env change, immediately `pip freeze > env/<name>_pinned_requirements.txt` and note the date, so results can be traced to a known package set.

When I say "upload to Google Drive" for a pptx / docx / pdf / html deliverable and give no folder, the default destination is the team deliverables folder via the rclone remote `drive:` with `--drive-root-folder-id <ID>`. Before uploading, list the folder and check for a file with the same name; don't overwrite someone else's file. Stage the files in one local folder, `rclone copy` the folder once, then verify with `rclone check --checksum --one-way <stage> drive: --drive-root-folder-id <ID>` and report the matching-file count. Never `--size-only`.

Codex sends the prompt and every file it reads to OpenAI. Fine for the user's own analyses; ask first for patient data, embargoed collaborator data, or anything the user marked sensitive. Verify every finding before applying it. Codex is a reviewer, not an oracle: open the cited file/line and confirm. In one past review all "must fix" items held up, but its suggested wording sometimes over-corrected; keep the author's voice and make the minimum effective edit.
